einzeiler: Preseason week two review with riser, faller and rookie insights for fantasy drafts.
kurzfassung: The hosts and Zane break down the second week of the NFL preseason, analyzing joint practices, training camp reports, and utilization data. They evaluate risers, fallers, and rookie performances to help managers refine their draft strategies. The discussion covers major offensive line concerns, backfield splits, and strategic late-round targets across multiple teams.
stichpunkte: Titan's offensive line struggles and Cam Ward's pressure issues.
Emmett Johnson as a late-round handcuff behind Kenneth Walker.
Malik Davis taking over the RB2 role for the Cowboys.
Bucky Irving's projection and role sharing with Kenneth Gainwell.
Kayshawn Booty traded to the Houston Texans, boosting Nico Collins.
Jordan Love and the Packers playing with faster tempo.
Backfield dynamics for the Denver Broncos with RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman.
Ashton Jeanty's injury situation pushing his draft stock down.

beschreibung:
Preseason box scores are close to worthless. Snap shares and route participation are not, and that's the whole difference between guessing and knowing.Zain Dhanani and Dwain McFarland go through Dwain's Week 2 preseason charting — who actually played, with whom, and on which downs — and pull out the situations that should move your draft board this week.The risers get most of the attention. MarShawn Lloyd looked like the clear RB2 in Green Bay and one of the better late-round backs on the board. De'Zhaun Stribling has moved into high-priority territory in San Francisco. KC Concepcion was reportedly the star of Cleveland's joint practices. Seth McGowan looks like the back to roster behind Jonathan Taylor, Ja'Kobi Lane is the favorite for Baltimore's WR3 job, and Jalen Royals, Tai Felton, Matthew Golden, Adonai Mitchell, Caleb Douglas and Malachi Fields all made cases for late-round roster spots.They also get to the guys trending the wrong way — Tyrone Tracy's usage in New York, Jaydon Blue's ball security in Dallas, Isaac TeSlaa's target problem in Detroit and a murky tight end picture in Los Angeles — plus the players who didn't suit up but whose stock still moved, including Tucker Kraft, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Dylan Sampson and Terrance Ferguson.Along the way: Colston Loveland's snap share and why he looks like a Round 4 cheat code, Christian Watson holding as one of the best picks in Rounds 5 and 6, Jaylen Waddle in Denver, Jonathon Brooks in Carolina, Kenneth Walker in Kansas City, Ladd McConkey with Justin Herbert, and Tetairoa McMillan's role in the Panthers offense.Read Dwain's full Week 2 charting here: https://www.fantasylife.com/articles/fantasy/nfl-preseason-week-2-takeaways-for-fantasy-footballTopics in this video:2026 fantasy football, NFL preseason, preseason week 2 takeaways, snap share, route participation, fantasy football draft strategy, MarShawn Lloyd, De'Zhaun Stribling, KC Concepcion, Seth McGowan, Ja'Kobi Lane, Jalen Royals, Tai Felton, Matthew Golden, Adonai Mitchell, Caleb Douglas, Colston Loveland, Christian Watson, Jaylen Waddle, Jonathon Brooks, Kenneth Walker, Ladd McConkey, Tetairoa McMillan, Tucker Kraft, Terrance Ferguson, Tyrone Tracy, Jaydon Blue, late round targets, fantasy football sleepers
